slice: Calibrate balanced same-plan A/A observations with the native randomized hasher

decision.scope: This is an A/A control of unchanged native plans. It is not a baseline/candidate comparison or validation of the original fresh-process measurement protocol.
decision.next_step: Any candidate timing claim must validate the controls and comparison in that candidate experiment. Do not transfer this within-process A/A interval to the earlier release-binary result.

method.question: Does adjacent, balanced native-plan replay yield a sufficiently precise A/A control without replacing the randomized hash implementation?
method.labels: Each native plan executes four times. The first/fourth occurrences are label A and the second/third label B, inverted for every odd (plan_index + label_flip). Label flip alternates by process pair. No candidate code or runtime mode differs between A and B.
method.statistics: Primary: per-process median of same-plan percentage changes between the means of two B executions and two A executions, then median across all eight processes of each mode. Secondary: per-process percentage change of full A/B means, then median across processes. 10000 whole-process bootstrap resamples, seed 88; no within-process independence claim.
method.calibration_target: Both primary and secondary conditional 95% intervals within +/-1%. Inspect any resolved nonzero bias separately. This target validates only A/A precision, not the candidate or the original fresh-plan benchmark.
method.stopping_rule: One fixed 16-process schedule, with all observations retained. No extensions until a preferred result.
limits: Sweep and adjacent modes use the same compiled executable. Both retain native randomized plans and allocations; only execution ordering changes.
No candidate versus baseline inference or absolute speed comparison against the prior replay executable.
No builds, tests or independent machine work during measurements.

source.identity: One executable for both schedules. Original type inference, native randomized hasher, accepted add-zero runtime. Production sources, dependency features/profiles and lockfile match the frozen before build.
source.restoration: All shared sources, lockfiles and executable slots are restored and hash checked.

limitations: Labels A and B execute the exact same retained plan; neither label enables the type-inference candidate.
Each plan has its own original randomized IN table. The four repeats share that table and its allocations, which differs from measuring a fresh plan once.
Balanced labels can cancel drift in both schedules. A pass by both modes does not establish that adjacency alone causes better precision.
The conditional intervals cover eight processes per mode on this host, not other workloads or hosts. No equivalence or universal zero-cost claim is made.
The earlier original-binary positive mean interval and failed self-comparison remain retained and unresolved by this A/A experiment.

reproduction.scripts: All scripts, capture data, counters and source/build identities are in the compressed record.
reproduction.setup: Extract into an empty sibling cache directory using the recorded frozen float-type-planning-f438591 sources. Recreate override.toml, paths.json, the dependency symlink and the benchmark source. Run sequentially; finish all builds and validation before measurement. The build helper restores shared files in finally.
